evidence: az-containerapp-show.json: ingress.traffic is a manual split — checkout-api--sv-3 (latest, v2.4.1) at 75% and checkout-api--sv-1 at 25%; the app is in multiple-revisions mode, so weights persist until changed
revision-list.json: sv-1 (image v2.3.9, the old pricing engine) is still active with trafficWeight 25; sv-2 is deactivated at 0; sv-3 runs v2.4.1 at 75
deploy-history.csv: the Oct 29 blue-green cutover was aborted at 50/50 and pinned by hand; the v2.4.1 deploy's traffic update zeroed sv-2 but never touched sv-1's pinned 25
support-tickets.log: the old fee appears for ~1 in 4 sessions, session-sticky, unaffected by restarts or redeploys — a routing ratio, not a replica or image problem
root_cause: The stale pricing is served by revision sv-1 (image v2.3.9), which still receives 25% of ingress traffic: the Oct 29 blue-green cutover was aborted at 50/50 and its weights were pinned manually, and the subsequent v2.4.1 deploy's traffic update zeroed sv-2 but left sv-1's pinned 25% in place. In multiple-revisions mode the ingress keeps splitting traffic by weight indefinitely — az-containerapp-show.json shows the live 75/25 split and revision-list.json shows sv-1 still active.
fix: Drain the old revision: set sv-3 to 100% of ingress traffic (az containerapp ingress traffic update --revision-weight checkout-api--sv-3=100, or --traffic-weight with latest-revision) and deactivate sv-1. Longer term: cut overs blue-green via single --target-port style cutover or ensure the deploy tooling zeroes ALL non-latest revision weights, and gate manual traffic pinning behind an explicit expiry so an aborted cutover cannot leak stale revisions into production.
